How it works

The grid starts at the selection's top left; a column is as wide as its widest object, a row as tall as its tallest. Rows: from the top down, an object shares a row when its centre lies within the row's height, or its top above the middle of an object in it. The last row may be short.

Objects keep the order they lie in on the page, and the first stays where it is. Gaps are between edges; centres are the middles of the boxes. Nothing is resized: a total too short for the objects is refused.

How it works

Nothing is read from the file: PNG and JPEG keep no microscope calibration, and their dpi is for printing. Take the pixel size from the microscope software or ImageJ (Image › Properties). The bar's length comes from it and the picture's size on the page, and is redrawn whenever the picture changes; a rotated picture needs square pixels.

  2. Click Add zoom inset
  3. Drag the box on the picture to choose the region

Region
Size
px
Zoom Box
More options
How it works

The region is kept in the picture's own pixels, so it stays on the same spot as the picture moves or scales; drag or resize the box (or crop the inset) to change it. The inset shows the embedded picture's own pixels, not a screenshot. The same region on other pictures is the same relative place in each, not an alignment of them.

  1. Select pictures
  2. Adjust
  3. Click Apply
Levels
Gamma Brightness Contrast
More options
Curve

Click to add a point, drag to move it, double-click to remove it.

How it works

The adjustment is an SVG filter on the picture (one lookup table per channel, ahead of any tint from Channels), so the pixels never change and Inkscape shows it too. Black and White are the same values as Min and Max under Channels. Gamma and curves are not linear: say so in the figure legend or methods when you submit.

  1. Select grayscale pictures
  2. Pick a colour and click Tint
  3. Or select 2–7 pictures and click Merge

More options
Range
Merge channels

Select 2 to 7 pictures of the same pixel size, in the order of their channels.

Blend
How it works

For showing, not for measuring: the colour and range are an SVG filter (the range, which is Adjust picture's Black and White, then grey by Rec. 709 weights, then the colour), and the pictures' pixels are never changed. Levels are those of the embedded 8-bit picture. Merging needs pictures of the same pixel size; they are overlaid pixel to pixel as they are, not registered, in a new group beside them.

svguest: I once paid for Adobe, then fell for open-source Inkscape, but at heart I've always loved lightweight tools, ideally ones that run right in the browser; now that AI is here, we can hand-craft the manual parts of our workflows exactly the way we want.

To start, add an API key for GLM or DeepSeek. Keys are kept in this browser; Models and keys shows how each service connects.

Context

What the AI read for the last reply: the whole chat goes with each message, other chats don't. Near the model's limit, the chat is summarised and continues in a new one that still edits the same figure.

Help

Getting started

  1. Open a figure. Ctrl+O, or drop an SVG from ggplot2, Inkscape or Illustrator onto the canvas. File › New starts a blank page.
  2. Select. Click a part; Ctrl+click takes its whole group; drag on an empty spot to box select.
  3. Edit. Drag to move, pull the handles to scale or rotate, double-click a text to retype it. The Properties panel on the right sets exact sizes, colours and fonts.
  4. Lay out. The FigKit menu sizes, aligns and labels panels, and adds scale bars and zoom insets.
  5. Save. Ctrl+S exports the SVG; the File menu also exports PDF, PNG and JPG.

Can't find a command? Ctrl+K searches all of them. Every change can be undone with Ctrl+Z.

SVG Chat

Model
Beside Send: the model that draws, its thinking, and which model reads images (Auto: the drawing model when it can, else one that can)
Models and keys
Your GLM or DeepSeek API key, tested when entered; TBtools' model needs none
Enter
Send; Shift+Enter new line
Chats
svguest opens on a new chat; the title switches to an earlier one, renames or deletes it; each is kept in this browser (Kept in this browser… saves them as files) and the AI reads only the current one; near the model's context limit a chat is summarised and continues in a new one
Attach
An image to redraw or a text file to draw from (or paste, drop)
Selection
Select objects first to ask about them or have them changed in place
Retry
Under the latest drawing: ask again, with this model or another
Long replies
Cut off at the token limit, they continue automatically, up to 3 times
Waiting
A seconds counter shows it is working; Stop cancels

FigKit

Size each
Give every selected object the same width or height, in proportion or stretched
Grid, align, space
Columns and gaps; edges or centres; the same gap, equal gaps or a total length; outlined before anything moves
Positions
Record where objects sit and put others there; swap two

A, B, C… and rectangles that follow their panels; run again to update them

From the pixel size you enter; redrawn when the picture changes

A box on a picture and its region enlarged; drag the box to change it

Levels, gamma, brightness, contrast and curves over the picture's histogram, previewed until Apply; the pixels are unchanged

Tint grayscale pictures (Min and Max are Adjust's Black and White); merge 2 to 7 channels

On a Mac, ⌘ works in place of Ctrl. Everything runs in your browser; only what you send to SVG Chat leaves it.

Copies svguest keeps for you between visits, in this browser only.

Open recent
SVG Chat
  • They sit in this site's own storage in the browser (IndexedDB: sgDocs, sgChats), not in a folder: a web page can't write to your disk by itself.
  • Download .zip saves the SVG copies, or each chat as a web page with its figures.
  • Each browser, private window, TBtools and downloaded copy of svguest keeps its own; clearing this site's data deletes them.
  • File › Auto-save turns the copies on or off; in Chrome or Edge, File › Auto-save to a folder also writes the open file into a folder you pick.
